# `Q-16-6` — Block shortcode in inline position

> A shortcode used inside a sentence produced block-level output, which
> could not be carried into the inline position and was dropped.

## What this means

Markdown content comes in two shapes. *Inline* content lives inside a
sentence — words, emphasis, links, code spans. *Block* content is
standalone: paragraphs, divs, raw HTML blocks, figures.

A shortcode can produce either, and where you put the invocation
decides which one fits. Written inside a sentence, the shortcode's
output has to be inline content, because that is the only thing that
can sit between two words.

The built-in `video` shortcode, for instance, produces a raw HTML
block. Placed mid-sentence, none of that output can be represented
inline, so it is dropped and this warning is reported.

The rest of your document renders normally; only the shortcode's
output is missing.

## Why this happens

- **The invocation is on the same line as other text.** Even a single
  leading word puts the shortcode in an inline position:

  ```markdown
  Watch: {{{< video https://youtu.be/example >}}}
  ```

- **The invocation is inside a list item, table cell, or heading**
  alongside other content.
- **A missing blank line.** A shortcode on its own line but directly
  adjacent to a paragraph above or below is part of that paragraph, and
  therefore inline.

## How to fix

Put the shortcode in its own paragraph, with blank lines on both
sides:

```markdown
Watch this:

{{{< video https://youtu.be/example >}}}

The rest of the section continues here.
```

The blank lines are what make it a block — this is ordinary markdown
paragraph separation, not a shortcode-specific rule.

If you need something inline, use a shortcode that produces inline
output. `{{{< meta ... >}}}`, `{{{< var ... >}}}`, and `{{{< env ... >}}}`
all substitute text and work anywhere.
